$comment: Single source of truth for every quality gate. scripts/validate-assets.mjs and the ship-check skill both read this file. Changing a number here changes the gate everywhere. Numbers are ceilings unless named *_min.

coreWebVitals.$comment: Field-realistic targets at p75 on a mid-tier Android over 4G, not lab-only numbers.

javascript.$comment: Gzipped. The 3D runtime MUST be a lazy chunk so it never counts against first load.

models.$comment: Per-file, AFTER geometry compression. Textures are resized rather than supercompressed: see requiredExtensions$comment.
models.maxGpuTextureMb$comment: Resident VRAM for all of a model's textures: width*height*4 bytes plus a third again for mipmaps. This is the number that decides whether a mid-tier phone keeps the tab alive, and it is invisible in download size — a 29KB PNG at 1024x640 costs 3.5MB here.
models.requiredExtensions$comment: Was [KHR_draco_mesh_compression, KHR_texture_basisu]. Both are unreachable on this site and the gate was therefore unsatisfiable: their decoders are Emscripten embind, and embind builds invoker functions at runtime with new Function. Our CSP forbids 'unsafe-eval' (lib/csp.ts), so both throw EvalError inside the decoder worker and the model silently never renders. meshoptimizer's decoder contains no eval and is the only geometry compression a strict CSP can run. Texture memory is controlled by the 512px clamp in scripts/optimize-gltf.sh instead — GPU cost is width*height*4, independent of the file size on disk.
models.forbiddenTextureFormats$comment: External texture references only. Embedded PNG/JPEG is permitted because KTX2 cannot be decoded under this site's CSP; dimensions and maxGpuTextureMb are the control.

prerenderedStills.$comment: The workhorse. Most 3D on the site is this, not live WebGL.

prerenderedVideo.$comment: Turntables and camera moves. Poster frame is mandatory so nothing pops in.

accessibility.$comment: Non-negotiable. A healthcare-education company shipping an inaccessible site is a credibility failure, not just a compliance one.
accessibility.contrastNormalText_min$comment: 7:1 is AAA and stricter than the AA this site conforms to. It is the brand kit's own body-text floor, and the kit's amended token values meet it, so the gate records the higher standard actually being held rather than the lower one that would also pass. tests/contrast.spec.ts parses the tokens straight out of app/globals.css and proves every pairing.
